metadata.note: The Rutland and Burlington Railroad (chartered 1843 as the Champlain & Connecticut River Rail Road, renamed 1847) -- Bellows Falls - Rutland - Burlington, opened through Dec 1849. Drawn as two legs, each split into one feature per operator era with identical geometry within a leg (Rule 4): Rutland & Burlington 1849-1867; first Rutland Railroad 1867-1870; Vermont Central lease 1871-1872; Central Vermont lease 1873-May 1896; Rutland Railroad / Rutland Railway May 1896 - June 26 1953 (Bellows Falls - Rutland only in this file -- Rutland - Burlington after 1891 is drawn by rutland_green_mountain_flyer.geojson). Year convention: segments are inclusive calendar years with no overlap between eras of the same leg; a mid-year handover year is drawn for the operator that ran the larger part of it (1867: R&B to July 8, so 1867 is R&B and the first Rutland Railroad is drawn from 1868; 1896: Rutland from May 7, so 1896 is Rutland's). The Jan 1 1871 lease and the Nov 2 1872 rename follow vermont_central_railroad.geojson's 1872/1873 boundary. Rule 4 decision (report UNRESOLVED 1): the 1867 reorganization is treated as a new company, so the Rutland and Burlington Railroad has its own colour for 1849-1867 and the first Rutland Railroad (1867-1870) takes the Rutland Railroad's colour pulled from rutland_green_mountain_flyer.geojson.
not_yet_sourced: Rutland - Burlington 1892 - May 1896: the Central Vermont lease actually ran to May 7 1896 (RRHS; Burlington Weekly Free Press May 7 1896), but cv-rutland-burlington-lease is drawn only to 1891 because rutland_green_mountain_flyer.geojson draws the leg from 1892. That Flyer feature colours 1892-1896 as the Rutland Railroad -- a Rule 4 split-at-ownership-change defect in that file, left for a follow-up.
amtrak.geojson 'Amtrak: Ethan Allen Express' draws Rutland - Burlington from 1996, but the extension to Burlington began July 2022 (report EXISTING LAYER CHECK) -- not fixed here.
Exact 1849 opening days: Bellows Falls - Chester between July 20 and Aug 3; Chester - Ludlow by Sept 27; the day the northern division reached Rutland (probably Oct 1849). Years are firm.
1896 return: RRHS says May 7; the Burlington Weekly Free Press wording leaves Thursday Apr 30 vs May 7 open.
Headways for 1850-1867 and for every era except Dec 1849 and 1951 are estimates; Pathfinder Guides of 1856 and 1866 would supply them.
No primary lease document seen for the 1867 reorganization or the 1871 lease; dates rest on the RRHS timeline.
Geometry: the R&B's own pre-1916 Burlington station and any 19th-century realignments (Rutland terminal layout, Burlington approach) are not traced; modern alignment drawn throughout.
omitted: Rutland - Burlington 1896-1953 (report block B5): already drawn by rutland_green_mountain_flyer.geojson.
Bellows Falls - Brattleboro, Vermont Valley lease 1865-1870 (C1): drawable NONE -- who ran the trains is unproven; belongs to a Vermont Valley layer.
Addison Branch and the 1870-71 leases (C2): drawable NONE here; first-Rutland leases, not R&B lines.
1849 stage connections (Ludlow - Rutland, Walpole - Brattleboro): road coaches, not rail.
Freight after June 26 1953 and Steamtown / Green Mountain Railroad excursions (Rule 1; separate operators).

segments.note: The Rutland & Burlington's southern division, opened in three pieces in 1849: Bellows Falls - Chester by early August (a Cheshire Railroad ad of July 23 1849, printed Aug 3, has the R&B 'now open to Chester', the July 20 ad does not mention it); Chester - Ludlow by Sept 27 1849 (Vermont Watchman: 'The Southern Division, from Bellows Falls to Ludlow, is also in operation'); and Ludlow - Rutland over the Mount Holly summit last, with a stage 'from Ludlow to cars, distance 23' miles in Oct-Nov 1849 (Rutland County Herald, Nov 14 1849) until the first through train of Dec 18 1849 (RRHS) and the 'THROUGH TO BELLOWS FALLS' timetable effective Monday Dec 24 1849 (Burlington Free Press, Jan 4 1850). Strictly, Ludlow - Rutland is proven only from December 1849; all of it is 1849. Boston passengers came up via the Cheshire and Fitchburg; from Nov 5 1849 they rode 'through from Ludlow to Boston without change of passenger or luggage cars'. Control passed to the Mortgage Trustees Nov 19 1853 but the road kept running under the R&B name -- not a change of operator. Ends 1867: the R&B was reorganized as the (first) Rutland Railroad effective July 9 1867; service continued without a break. Headway: the Dec 1849 timetable shows one through Burlington - Boston train each way, Sundays excepted -- that month only; later R&B years are NOT sourced, so 1440 is an estimate for 1850-1867. 1850 Pathfinder stops (branchline.uk letter x) at Rockingham, Chester, Gassetts, Duttonsville, Proctorsville, Ludlow, Mount Holly, Cuttingsville, Clarendon. Year convention: segments are inclusive calendar years with no overlap between eras of the same leg; a mid-year handover year is drawn for the operator that ran the larger part of it (1867: R&B to July 8, so 1867 is R&B and the first Rutland Railroad is drawn from 1868; 1896: Rutland from May 7, so 1896 is Rutland's). The Jan 1 1871 lease and the Nov 2 1872 rename follow vermont_central_railroad.geojson's 1872/1873 boundary.
sources: Segment-level: the 1849 openings are from the contemporary newspapers below (Vermont Phoenix Aug 1849, Vermont Watchman Sept 27 1849, Rutland County Herald Nov 1849 / Jan 1850, Burlington Free Press Jan 4 1850); the Dec 18 1849 through train, Nov 19 1853 trustees and July 9 1867 reorganization are from the RRHS timeline; 1850 stops from branchline.uk. The headway after Dec 1849 is NOT sourced.

segments.note: The Rutland was leased to its old rival, the Vermont Central, for 20 years from Jan 1 1871 (lease signed Dec 30 1870, RRHS). The Vermont Central now worked both cross-state routes, Windsor - Burlington and Bellows Falls - Burlington. Ends 1872: the lessee was renamed the Central Vermont Railroad Nov 2 1872 (same 1872/1873 boundary as vermont_central_railroad.geojson). No primary lease document seen. Headway estimated.

segments.note: Central Vermont lease era: the Central Vermont Railroad from the Nov 2 1872 rename, and from Jan 1 1891 the Central Vermont Railway under a 99-year renewal (company string kept as 'Central Vermont Railway' for the whole succession, as in vermont_central_railroad.geojson). Positive evidence of CV operation mid-lease: branchline.uk's Rutland legend 'z: 1893(CV)t' -- the 1893 snapshot of these stations is a CENTRAL VERMONT public timetable; leg-11 stations also carry 'y' (1876 Pathfinder). The lease ended on the CV receivership: the Rutland took its road back on Thursday May 7 1896 (RRHS; Burlington Weekly Free Press May 7 1896, 'CLEMENT TAKES HIS ROAD'; the weekly's wording leaves Apr 30 vs May 7 open). Drawn to 1895 under this layer's year convention (the Rutland ran most of 1896). Headway estimated. Year convention: segments are inclusive calendar years with no overlap between eras of the same leg; a mid-year handover year is drawn for the operator that ran the larger part of it (1867: R&B to July 8, so 1867 is R&B and the first Rutland Railroad is drawn from 1868; 1896: Rutland from May 7, so 1896 is Rutland's). segments.note: The Rutland Railroad again, from May 7 1896 (Rutland Railway Corp. from Nov 1 1950 -- a reorganization, not a new operator; NYC and New Haven stock control 1904-1941 were shareholders, not operators). Operating proof of the return: on May 18 1896 a Rutland conductor refused a Central Vermont mileage ticket between Bellows Falls and Chester (Burlington Weekly Free Press May 21 1896). The Boston - Montreal route: B&M sections from Boston via Keene ran through as Rutland trains -- the Feb 1952 Official Guide (eff. Sept 30 1951) Table 3 shows times at Bellows Falls, Chester and Gassetts for the Mount Royal (143-51 / 52-146) and the Green Mountain (165-65 / 64-164), and lists Ludlow and Proctorsville without a dagger -- 1951 service CONFIRMED. branchline.uk letters every intermediate station on this leg only to 1932 and never 1953; the 1951 Guide and the April 26 1953 public timetable disprove a 1930s end -- a branchline.uk omission. Ends with the strike of June 26 1953; passenger service never resumed (RRHS). Freight continued under the Rutland to Sept 1961 and under Vermont Railway / Green Mountain Railroad since -- not drawn (Rule 1). Steamtown and Green Mountain Railroad excursions are separate tourist operators, not this feature. Headway 720 = the two daily through trains each way in the 1951 Guide, that year only; other years estimated. Year convention: segments are inclusive calendar years with no overlap between eras of the same leg; a mid-year handover year is drawn for the operator that ran the larger part of it (1867: R&B to July 8, so 1867 is R&B and the first Rutland Railroad is drawn from 1868; 1896: Rutland from May 7, so 1896 is Rutland's). The Jan 1 1871 lease and the Nov 2 1872 rename follow vermont_central_railroad.geojson's 1872/1873 boundary.

segments.note: The R&B's northern division, opened north to south: Burlington - Salisbury, 40 mi, on Thursday Sept 20 1849 (Vermont Watchman Sept 27 1849, 'opened on Thursday last'; the Charlotte News 2021 history has the Burlington Free Press printing the first schedule on Oct 5 1849), then on to Rutland and Clarendon by the standing ad set 'Nov. 1849' (Rutland County Herald: 'now opened to Clarendon, a distance of 74 miles from Burlington', passenger train from Burlington 8 a.m., and a 'freight train with passenger car attached' Rutland 3.30 a.m. - Burlington 11 a.m.). The exact day Rutland was reached (probably October 1849) was not found; the year is safe. Through to Bellows Falls Dec 18 1849 (RRHS), with an accommodation train Rutland 7.30 a.m. - Burlington from Dec 24 1849 (Burlington Free Press). The R&B was carrying Burlington passengers three months before the Vermont Central reached the city (Dec 31 1849). Its terminus was its own Burlington station, not the 1916 Union Station (see geometry_quality). Mortgage Trustees from Nov 19 1853, same railroad -- not a split. Ends 1867 with the July 9 1867 reorganization as the Rutland Railroad. Headway: roughly two trains each way per weekday in Nov-Dec 1849 from the two ads; 1850-1867 NOT sourced, estimate. Year convention: segments are inclusive calendar years with no overlap between eras of the same leg; a mid-year handover year is drawn for the operator that ran the larger part of it (1867: R&B to July 8, so 1867 is R&B and the first Rutland Railroad is drawn from 1868; 1896: Rutland from May 7, so 1896 is Rutland's). The Jan 1 1871 lease and the Nov 2 1872 rename follow vermont_central_railroad.geojson's 1872/1873 boundary.

The headway after Dec 1849 is NOT sourced.
